title: Which amount, and what it holds

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `LocalDate.of(2024, 1, 15).plus(Duration.ofDays(30))` do?

options.text: It returns 2024-02-14, thirty days after the date
options.says: The page shows this call failing: a LocalDate has no time, so it cannot take a seconds-based Duration; thirty days on a date is plusDays(30).

options.text: It throws UnsupportedTemporalTypeException at run time
options.says: The page marks this exact call with UnsupportedTemporalTypeException and says to use a Period for date arithmetic.

options.text: It returns 2024-02-15, one calendar month after the date
options.says: One calendar month is what the page's fix, plus(Period.ofMonths(1)), gives; the Duration call itself fails.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `Period.of(1, 2, 3).getDays()` return?

options.says: 2 is the months component, which getMonths() returns; the page says each component is stored and read on its own.
The page says months have variable lengths, so a Period cannot turn its months into days on its own.
The page says getDays() returns only the days component, 3 here, not a total.
